correctness.rationale: The Clebsch–Gordan rule plus Haar orthonormality gives the exact fourth-moment polynomial; its coefficientwise positivity reduces the unrestricted complex maximum to nonnegative magnitudes. The odd and even leading angular forms have unique nondegenerate interior maxima; stationarity rigorously yields an optimal trivial-mode amplitude \(R_*/(nf_*)+O(n^{-2})\) and norm gain \(2R_*^2/(nf_*)+O(n^{-2})\). Explicit algebra gives the stated constants. The finite exact fusion checks and numerical stress cases are only corroborative. Independent class-angle Haar quadrature agrees with the fusion formula on 12 complex-coefficient test cases.

value.rationale: The first nonzero cost-benefit law for introducing the trivial \(SU(2)\) representation into a sparse high-weight Fourier packet is an exact, naturally posed sensitivity invariant. Both parity classes have nonzero sharp \(1/n\) gains and different limiting high-mode proportions, while the optimizer assigns the low mode weight of precise order \(1/n\). The result holds for an infinite sequence and is not a table recomputation or simple baseline renormalization.
